items.prompt: Two streams share their most recent k prices but differ before that window. Which comparison is valid?

options.text: Their fixed-window means must differ forever.
options.why: Expired observations have zero weight in a fixed window, so earlier history cannot affect its current mean.

options.text: Their recursive EMAs must be identical.
options.why: A recursive EMA can retain a decaying contribution from earlier history; identical recent windows do not force identical state.

options.text: Both methods ignore order and all earlier values.
options.why: EMA is recursive and order-sensitive. Even the window must select the correct active observations.

options.text: Their fixed-window means agree; their EMAs can differ.
options.why: A fixed window discards expired history entirely, while an EMA generally retains decayed prior state.

items.explanation: A fixed window discards expired history entirely, while an EMA generally retains decayed prior state.
